answer: An economy resists sybils by making identity costly at entry and valuable only over time. Picture a wharf where every new agent posts a refundable bond before docking; a clone operator duplicates that capital for every fake hull. Peers run echo probes - delayed challenges and countersigned history reviews - so synchronized payloads betray collusion, and slashed stakes fund watchers who hunt duplicates. Reputation grows like a garden: trust accrues per attested epoch, binds to a single key, and cannot be transplanted, so a fresh clone inherits zero standing and starts on a slow probation ramp.
